title: Surendra

card.teaser: A typeface drawn from old wood and metal type specimens. Every heading on this site is set in it.

summary: A custom serif typeface inspired by historical wood and metal type, developed through distinctive letterforms, wedge serifs, and expressive details.

hero.alt: An open magazine with the headline "It was raining inside" set in Surendra.

text: Surendra explores how the character of historical type can be translated into a contemporary digital typeface. The focus is on the construction of the letterforms themselves: their proportions, terminals, contrast, and the small irregularities that give a typeface its personality.
The project combines type research, letterform development, and specimen design to explore how historical references can inform a contemporary typeface.

rows.heading: Starting from old type
rows.body: I collected wood and metal type specimens and marked them up in red pen. What I kept noticing was how physical the letters feel: uneven weight, soft corners and ink spreading at the edges. I wanted that character without copying any one archival face.
rows.caption: Type specimens and annotations.

rows.heading: Drawing the glyph set
rows.body: I drew the letters by hand first, using "Type Cooker" as my test line and redrawing it until the shapes felt like one family. Then I rebuilt them digitally and worked through spacing and kerning, checking that every character belonged.
rows.caption: Glyph sketches.
rows.alt: Hand sketches and digital iterations for Surendra glyphs.

finalDesign: The specimens had heavy ink spread and uneven weight, which looks great in a headline and rough in a paragraph. I kept the soft corners and wedge serifs, evened out the weight and lowered the contrast so the face could still set text. The slanted *e* and the curled *7* are the two quirks I left in on purpose. Everything else stays quiet, so those two do the remembering.
pull: Heavy ink looks great in a headline and rough in a paragraph.
